about: Weekly Prep'Up reel pipeline. One video per Buffer slot, queued to TikTok, Instagram and Facebook. Every video gets a music combination (style + key) never used before.
lessons: « 6 outils » reel (29 Oct): average watch time 3 s of 31.5 s (TikTok and Instagram). The hook must show motion or a number in the first second, never a text-only screen. Keep videos 15-22 s.
TikTok gets about 10x Instagram's views: always include it.
10 Nov: no new video published since the 6-tools reel, so no new evidence. The first real comparison comes after Wednesday's Rank calculator reel.

12 Nov (preliminary, 14 h of data): a rolling-number hook and a 21 s length raised the watch share (9.5% → 13.5% on TikTok) but not the seconds watched (~3 s both times). Viewers decide in the first 1-2 s, before the hook plays out, so the very first frame has to grab them.
Posting through Buffer in the Wed 20:00 slot reached 548 TikTok views in 14 h: timing and posting route are not the problem; holding attention is.

14 Nov (2 videos, 2.5+ days of data each): number hook + 21 s beat text hook + 31.5 s on reach (641 vs 611 TikTok views in a fraction of the time) and watch share (15.2% vs 9.4%), but the seconds watched barely moved (3.2 s vs 3.0 s). Shorter videos help the share; the first 2 seconds are still the bottleneck. Evidence is thin: 2 videos.

Zero comments after 2 videos and 6 posts: the comment CTAs at the end of the captions are not working, probably because people leave before reading. Instagram reach and watch time are far below TikTok's (22 vs 641 views).

19 Nov: Places (static poster frame + app) fell to 1.7 s average watch on TikTok after 16 h, vs ~3.3 s for Target grades. A still first screen loses viewers; open on the payoff with motion. Question-style caption first line (Target grades) brought the first shares (2), still 0 comments.
Buffer free plan: first comments are not available (paid feature), so the pinned-comment experiment cannot be automated.

analytics.how: Before each new video: pull sent posts with metrics from Buffer, record them per video and platform, compare videos, then update 'lessons' and 'strategy'. Metrics refresh about daily: treat posts younger than 48 h as preliminary.
metrics_tracked: avg watch time (s) and % of video length

history.verdict: Stable since 9 Nov (TikTok 598 → 600 views): the reel has stopped spreading. Viewers still leave at ~3 s (9.5% of 31.5 s on TikTok, 12.1% on Instagram). Still the only published video, so there is nothing to compare yet.

history.verdict: After 2.5 days it has passed the 6-tools reel's 16-day TikTok total (641 vs 611 views). Watch share 15.2% vs 9.4% (+5.8 pts), but seconds watched only 3.2 vs 2.96 (+0.24 s): the shorter length explains most of the gain; viewers still leave around 3 s. Instagram is weak (22 views, 1.4 s watched); Facebook is steady (~220 impressions). Still zero comments on both videos.

Target grades (question as caption first line, 17 s) held 3.3 s and got the first 2 shares. Places (static number poster + app from frame 0) fell to 1.7 s after 16 h: a still first screen loses people. Next: open on the payoff already in motion.

dashboard.note: After each run: python3 toolkit/dashboard_files.py, then upload_asset videos.json and strategie.json and update datasets/videos and datasets/strategie with the new urls and updated.at.

langue: Write lessons, strategy, experiments, changelog and the dashboard fields (nom, accroche, musique) in English: they are shown as-is on the user's dashboard. Post captions stay in French for the audience.

tiktok_route.route: Buffer, like Instagram and Facebook. Music is now inside the videos, so no TikTok in-app sound is needed. The PC scheduled task "Prep'Up TikTok posting" is DISABLED; do not use it.
tiktok_route.slideshows: TikTok photo slideshows: queue in Buffer with schedulingType "notification" (Buffer reminder). At the slot Rayen gets a notification, finishes the post in the TikTok phone app with a trending sound of his choice, and posts it himself. Videos (music inside) stay automatic.

beat_sync.method: Videos for TikTok: pick a trending song (tokchart.com / charts), get its measured beat positions (AcousticBrainz low-level API, by MusicBrainz id), choose a start second where a beat falls within ~15 ms and tempo is steady, write the real beat times relative to that start into a beats JSON, render with BEATMAP=<json> node render.cjs (composition beat k at 0.5 s is shown exactly on real beat k), upload silent, and put tiktok.sound {search, artist, start_at} so the PC task adds that exact sound at that start point. Never embed the song audio. UPDATE 15 Nov: TikTok library sounds are ~1:00 clips at an unknown point in the song, so the start point cannot be set exactly. The video is tempo-matched to the measured beats; the PC task adds the official sound and stops, and Rayen drags the sound by ear so the first cut hits a beat, then clicks Schedule (tempo match keeps all later cuts on the beat).
beat_sync.status: replaced on 2026-11-15 by music_method (music generated inside the video); kept for reference

music_method.rule: No default style. For each new video: check what is viral on TikTok that week (tokchart.com US + worldwide), pick a song whose energy fits the video, write an ACE-Step caption describing its STYLE only (genre, groove, instruments, energy; never the title, artist, lyrics or melody), generate 2-3 candidates at the video grid BPM (120) with toolkit/gen_music.py, fit with toolkit/fit_music.py, keep the one with the clearest beat, and note inspired_by in the video entry. Different style from the previous videos when possible.
music_method.why: Rayen: music must feel like current viral songs; audience disliked the generic synth tracks; TikTok library sounds could not be synced.
